title: Systematic and Scoping Reviews — PRISMA, Risk of Bias and GRADE

hook.en: A narrative review is one expert's tour of the literature. A systematic review is a repeatable investigation with a written plan, a complete search and a fair judgement of every study. Learn how to tell them apart, and how to judge whether a review deserves your trust.
hook.ur: Narrative review ek maahir ka literature ka daura hai. Systematic review ek dohraya ja sakne wali tehqiq hai jis ka likha hua plan, mukammal search aur har study ka munsifana jaiza hota hai. Seekhein dono ko kaise alag karein, aur kaise parkhein ke review aap ke bharose ke qabil hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll distinguish narrative, systematic and scoping reviews, follow the PRISMA flow of a review, know what RoB 2 and ROBINS-I assess, and explain how GRADE rates the certainty of the evidence.
goal.ur: End tak aap narrative, systematic aur scoping reviews mein farq karenge, review ke PRISMA flow ko follow karenge, jaanenge RoB 2 aur ROBINS-I kya parakhte hain, aur samjhayenge ke GRADE saboot ki yaqeeniyat kaise rate karta hai.

text.en: A **systematic review** answers a focused question by searching for all relevant studies using a **written protocol**, selecting them with set criteria, assessing their **risk of bias** and synthesising the results, with or without a meta-analysis. A **scoping review** maps what research exists on a broad topic, without judging quality in depth. The **PRISMA 2020** statement sets out what a review report should contain, including a **flow diagram** showing how many records were found, screened and included. **GRADE** rates how certain we are about each key outcome.
text.ur: **Systematic review** ek markooz sawal ka jawab **likhe hue protocol** se tamam mutaliq studies dhoondh kar, tay shuda criteria se chun kar, un ke **risk of bias** ka jaiza le kar aur nateeje jama kar ke deta hai, meta-analysis ke saath ya baghair. **Scoping review** wasi mauzu par maujood research ka naqsha banata hai, quality ka gehra jaiza liye baghair. **PRISMA 2020** statement batata hai ke review ki report mein kya hona chahiye, jis mein **flow diagram** bhi hai jo dikhata hai kitne records mile, chhante gaye aur shamil hue. **GRADE** rate karta hai ke har ahem nateeje ke baare mein hum kitne yaqeeni hain.

text.en: Think of **a detective's case file versus a newspaper story**. The newspaper tells an interesting story from the sources the writer chose. The case file lists every witness, how each was found, how reliable each is and how they fit together. A systematic review is the case file. A scoping review is the map of where all the witnesses live.
text.ur: **Jasoos ki case file aur akhbar ki kahani** sochein. Akhbar un zarai se dilchasp kahani sunata hai jo likhne wale ne chune. Case file har gawah ka zikr karti hai, kaise mila, kitna bharosemand hai aur kaise mel khata hai. Systematic review case file hai. Scoping review us naqshe jaisa hai jo batata hai tamam gawah kahan rehte hain.

question.en: A review pools 15 trials, but 12 have a high risk of bias and the pooled estimate is imprecise. How would GRADE likely rate the certainty?
question.ur: Review 15 trials mila deta hai, lekin 12 ka risk of bias zyada hai aur pooled andaaza ghair durust hai. GRADE yaqeeniyat ko kaise rate karega?

text.en: Not rated, because it is a review

text.en: **Equating "systematic" with "good".** A systematic review can still be poor: no registered protocol, a narrow search, no risk-of-bias assessment, or pooling studies that should not be pooled. Look at the protocol registration (for example PROSPERO), the search, the risk-of-bias judgement and whether conclusions follow the certainty of the evidence. Another trap is the conclusion "more research is needed" with no statement of what is currently known.
text.ur: **"Systematic" ko "achha" samajhna.** Systematic review phir bhi kharab ho sakta hai: registered protocol nahi, tang search, risk-of-bias ka jaiza nahi, ya aisi studies jinhein nahi milana chahiye thi ka milana. Protocol registration (masalan PROSPERO), search, risk-of-bias ka faisla aur is baat ko dekhein ke nateeje saboot ki yaqeeniyat ke mutabiq hain ya nahi. Ek aur jaal "mazeed research chahiye" ka nateeja hai jis mein yeh bayan na ho ke abhi kya maloom hai.

text.en: **Read the "summary of findings" first.** Good reviews include a table with the main outcomes, effect sizes and GRADE certainty. If it says "moderate certainty, small to moderate benefit", you can tell a patient clearly what to expect, and why. For quick appraisal, ask: was there a protocol, a full search, a risk-of-bias judgement and a sensible reason for pooling?
text.ur: **Pehle "summary of findings" parhein.** Achhe reviews mein ahem nateejon, effect sizes aur GRADE yaqeeniyat ki table hoti hai. Agar kehti hai "darmiyani yaqeeniyat, chhota se darmiyana faida" to aap mareez ko saaf bata sakte hain ke kya umeed rakhein, aur kyun. Tez jaiza ke liye poochhein: protocol tha, mukammal search tha, risk-of-bias ka faisla tha aur milane ki munasib wajah thi?

question.en: What do RoB 2 and ROBINS-I assess?
question.ur: RoB 2 aur ROBINS-I kya parakhte hain?

answer.en: RoB 2 assesses the risk of bias in randomised trials across five areas: randomisation, deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, outcome measurement and selection of the reported result. ROBINS-I assesses non-randomised studies of interventions across seven areas, including confounding, selection of participants and classification of interventions, by comparing the study with an ideal target trial.
answer.ur: RoB 2 randomised trials ka risk of bias paanch hissoon mein parakhta hai: randomisation, irada kiye gaye ilajon se inhiraf, ghayab nateeje ka data, nateeje ki pemaish aur shaya shuda nateeje ka intikhab. ROBINS-I ilaaj ki non-randomised studies ko saat hissoon mein parakhta hai, confounding, shirkat karne walon ka intikhab aur ilajon ki daraja-bandi samet, study ko ek munasib target trial se milakar.

beats.patient: A therapist reads a headline: "Review proves dry needling works for neck pain." She opens the review and finds 8 small trials, most with high risk of bias, a pooled benefit of 6 points (95 percent CI 1 to 11), no protocol registration and "low certainty" in the summary table.
beats.assessment: The review is systematic in form, but the evidence behind it is weak, and the benefit is small and imprecise.
beats.treatment: She tells her colleagues that the review shows a possible small short-term effect with low certainty, and does not change her practice on this alone.
beats.reassess: She discusses the evidence honestly with a patient who asks, and offers dry needling as an optional adjunct alongside exercise.

text.en: **A review's conclusions are only as safe as the data on harm.** Check whether the review looked at adverse events. If it did not, or the included trials did not report them, safety is unknown, not proven. For techniques with known serious but rare risks, search separately for harm data and case reports.
text.ur: **Review ke nateeje utne hi mehfooz hain jitna nuqsan ka data.** Dekhein ke review ne adverse events dekhe ya nahi. Agar nahi, ya shamil trials ne report nahi kiye, to safety na-maloom hai, sabit nahi. Aisi techniques ke liye jin ke maloom seriyas lekin nadir khatre hon, nuqsan ka data aur case reports alag dhoondhein.

text.en: The PRISMA 2020 statement updated the reporting guideline for systematic reviews, with a 27-item checklist and flow diagram to improve transparency about how reviews are conducted and reported. ROBINS-I provides a structured tool to assess risk of bias in non-randomised studies of interventions by comparing each study with a hypothetical randomised trial, and GRADE treats evidence from non-randomised studies as starting at low certainty, which may be raised or lowered.
text.ur: PRISMA 2020 statement ne systematic reviews ke liye reporting guideline update kiya, 27 items ki checklist aur flow diagram ke saath taake reviews kaise chalaye aur report kiye jate hain us mein shaffafiyat barhe. ROBINS-I interventions ki non-randomised studies mein risk of bias parakhne ka munazzam aala deta hai, har study ko ek farzi randomised trial se milakar, aur GRADE non-randomised studies ke saboot ko kam yaqeeniyat se shuru karta hai, jo barhayi ya ghatayi ja sakti hai.

text.en: **Protocol, Search, Judge, Grade.** A good review has a protocol, a full search, a fair judgement of each study and a GRADE rating.
text.ur: **Protocol, Search, Jaiza, Grade.** Achhe review mein protocol, mukammal search, har study ka munsifana jaiza aur GRADE rating hoti hai.

summary.en: Systematic reviews follow a protocol and fair methods; scoping reviews map a broad topic.
summary.ur: Systematic reviews protocol aur munsifana tareeqe follow karte hain; scoping reviews wasi mauzu ka naqsha banate hain.

summary.en: PRISMA guides reporting, RoB 2 and ROBINS-I assess bias and GRADE rates certainty.
summary.ur: PRISMA report ki rehnumai karta hai, RoB 2 aur ROBINS-I bias parakhte hain aur GRADE yaqeeniyat rate karta hai.

summary.en: Do not trust a review just because it is "systematic"; check protocol, search, bias and certainty.
summary.ur: Review ko sirf "systematic" hone par na maanein; protocol, search, bias aur yaqeeniyat dekhein.
